title: Trying again after losing a baby | NHS inform
text:
Trying again after losing a baby
The decision about when and if to try for another baby after a loss is a personal one.
Some people want to try again quickly. Others feel they need some time to prepare themselves emotionally. There’s no right or wrong way to approach it.
It may be helpful to speak to your doctor, nurse or midwife before trying to get pregnant again. They can explain if there’s any medical reasons why you should wait.
When to start trying again after baby loss
Even if you feel emotionally ready, it’s important to wait until your body is physically ready.
You should not have sex until all symptoms of your baby loss have gone. This includes symptoms like bleeding or pain.
It’s generally recommended to wait until you’ve had 1 period before getting pregnant again. This allows you to date the next pregnancy and have early scans.
If you do become pregnant before having a period, there’s no need to worry. There’s no increased risk to this pregnancy. It just makes it a little harder for you to date the pregnancy.
Medical reasons to wait
There may be some medical reasons why you should wait.
If you’ve had a
molar pregnancy
, you should not become pregnant until the end of your follow up appointments.
Read more about pregnancy after molar pregnancy
If you’ve had an ectopic pregnancy, the amount of time you should wait depends on the treatment you had. This could be between 2 and 6 months. The doctor, nurse or midwife treating you will confirm exactly how long you should wait.
Your next pregnancy
If you do get pregnant again, you may find that you’re more anxious this time.
You should register with maternity services as soon as possible. During your first appointment, you should tell the midwife about your previous loss.
At this time, the midwife will discuss with you how you’d like to refer to your loss. You may have a name or gender you wish them to use during discussions. You can also ask not to discuss your loss unless absolutely necessary. This will be noted on your records, so you’ll not need to keep recalling your experience.
If you’ve experienced baby loss, you may be offered extra antenatal care. This could be additional appointments and more scans. These are not offered to everyone who has experienced baby loss. If you need extra scans and appointments, those treating you will explain why.
